description: Monitors cgroups v2 memory pressure signals — memory.events (oom_kill, high, max counters) and Pressure Stall Information (PSI) via /proc/pressure/memory — to detect resource leaks before they exhaust system memory. When a cgroup approaches its memory limit due to a resource leak, these interfaces provide deterministic signals (memory.high threshold crossings, oom_kill increments, PSI stall percentages) that monitoring systems consume to trigger alerts and automated remediation. Complements cgroup memory limits (CME-704) which contain the leak by adding detection of when containment is being stressed. The memory.events counters are monotonically increasing and per-cgroup, enabling precise attribution of pressure to the leaking workload.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Compensating control: cgroup memory pressure events (memory.events oom_kill/high counters and PSI stall metrics) provide deterministic early warning of resource leaks before system-wide exhaustion occurs, enabling operators to identify and remediate leaking processes within the monitoring interval — the attacker must exhaust resources faster than the monitoring and response cycle to achieve sustained denial of service.

verification.method: Check that cgroup memory.events is accessible and PSI is enabled in the kernel

commands.expected: Non-zero counters if pressure has occurred; file existence confirms cgroup v2 memory accounting is active
PSI metrics present (some/full avg10/avg60/avg300 values); confirms CONFIG_PSI=y

remediation.name: systemd PSI memory pressure monitor with journal alerting

steps.description: Create a shell script that reads PSI avg10 and alerts via systemd-cat when memory pressure exceeds a threshold (default 25%)
steps.command:
printf '#!/bin/bash
THRESHOLD=${1:-25}
while true; do
  PRESSURE=$(awk "/^some/ {split(\$2,a,"="); printf "%%d", a[2]}" /proc/pressure/memory)
  if [ "$PRESSURE" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "ALERT: memory pressure avg10=${PRESSURE}%% exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}%%" | systemd-cat -t cme-1010-psi -p warning
  fi
  sleep 10
done
' > /usr/local/bin/cme-1010-psi-monitor.sh && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cme-1010-psi-monitor.sh

steps.description: Create a script that polls memory.events for oom_kill increments on a target service's cgroup and logs warnings
steps.command:
printf '#!/bin/bash
SVC=${1:?"Usage: $0 <service-name>"}
CG=/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/${SVC}.service/memory.events
test -f "$CG" || { echo "No cgroup at $CG"; exit 1; }
PREV_OOM=$(awk "/oom_kill/ {print \$2}" "$CG")
while true; do
  CUR_OOM=$(awk "/oom_kill/ {print \$2}" "$CG")
  if [ "$CUR_OOM" -gt "$PREV_OOM" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "ALERT: ${SVC} oom_kill count increased ${PREV_OOM}->${CUR_OOM}" | systemd-cat -t cme-1010-oom -p err
    PREV_OOM=$CUR_OOM
  fi
  sleep 5
done
' > /usr/local/bin/cme-1010-oom-watch.sh && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cme-1010-oom-watch.sh

steps.description: Create a systemd service template that watches memory.events for any specified service
steps.command:
printf '[Unit]
Description=CME-1010 cgroup memory.events oom_kill watcher for %%i
After=sysinit.target %s

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/cme-1010-oom-watch.sh %%i
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10s

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
' > /etc/systemd/system/cme-1010-oom-watch@.service

steps.description: Enable the oom_kill watcher for a target service (replace <service> with the service name, e.g. httpd)
